sents.t: With Lily’s bakery opening in January, I knew it was the right time.
I bought an engagement ring.
It’s small and simple, but I saved for months to buy it.
I hid the little box in my sock drawer and planned to propose on Christmas Eve.
But on December 20th, the ring was gone.
I searched everywhere: under the bed, in my pockets, in the car.
“Someone must have taken it!” I said to Rosa.
“Nobody has a key to your apartment except me,” she said.
“It can’t have been stolen. You might have moved it.”
Then I remembered.
I had taken the ring out to look at it on the sofa.
Max had been sitting next to me.
We looked at Max.
Max looked at us.
He wagged his tail and looked away.
“He couldn’t have eaten it,” Rosa said.
“The box is too big. But he loves to hide things.”
We searched Max’s bed, and there, between a sock, a tennis ball, and one of Rosa’s gloves, was the little velvet box.
The ring was inside, perfectly safe.
“Max must have thought it was a toy,” Rosa laughed.
Then her eyes went wide.
“Wait. A ring? Sam!”
I put my finger to my lips.
“Shh. It’s a secret until Christmas Eve.”
